title: Azure Functions Queue Trigger Backlog and Failures

controlTest.positiveScenario: Inject sample events matching UC-4.5.6 SPL; confirm the search returns rows and alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign traffic without matching markers; confirm UC-4.5.6 search returns zero rows.

dataSources: `index=azure` sourcetype=`mscs:azure:metrics` collected via `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices`; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:metrics" (metricName="QueueMessageCount" OR metricName="ActiveMessages")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.6_azure_functions_queue_tr_6"
| sort -_time
description: Queue-triggered functions depend on storage or Service Bus depth; growing backlogs mean consumers cannot keep pace or messages are poisoned.
value: Detecting azure functions queue trigger backlog and failures early reduces mean time to contain cloud incidents, supports audit logging controls, and prevents silent misconfiguration drift across accounts.
implementation: Ingest queue depth metrics for the storage account or Service Bus namespace backing the trigger. Correlate with FunctionAppLogs for dequeue/processing errors. Alert when depth exceeds threshold or poison-message handling spikes. Map queue resource to Function App via tags or a lookup.
visualization: Dual-axis line chart (queue depth vs successful executions), Table (queue, depth, errors), Single value (oldest message age if exported).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as agg_value
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.CPU
  by Performance.host span=5m
| sort - agg_value
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (CPU node).
knownFalsePositives: Short spikes at deploy time, autoscale thrash, or a noisy neighbor on shared hosts can look bad for a few minutes. We require the condition to last across several intervals or clear on its own before we wake someone.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=azure`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` with the modular input for `mscs:azure:metrics`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.5.16.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `userIdentity.arn` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest queue depth metrics for the storage account or Service Bus namespace backing the trigger. Correlate with FunctionAppLogs for dequeue/processing errors. Alert when depth exceeds threshold or poison-message handling spikes. Map queue resource to Function App via tags or a lookup.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:metrics" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=azure sourcetype="mscs:azure:metrics" (metricName="QueueMessageCount" OR metricName="ActiveMessages")
| table _time userIdentity.arn eventName sourceIPAddress
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.5.6_azure_functions_queue_tr_6"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `mscs:azure:metrics` in `index=azure` to detect azure functions queue trigger backlog and failures. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `userIdentity.arn` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_5_6_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Dual-axis line chart (queue depth vs successful executions), Table (queue, depth, errors), Single value (oldest message age if exported)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_microsoft-cloudservices` and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of azure functions queue trigger backlog and failures so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
